chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham bin Salim, from Moalla bin Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Says: 'He has opposed Me, the one who humiliates My Momin servant'.

key_terms.نَابَذَنِي: He has opposed Me / declared war on Me

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when Allah says He has been opposed by one who humiliates a believer?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith utilizes the Qudsi format to elevate the status of the believer (abd Allah) to a direct mirror of God’s own dignity, implying that slighting a believer is tantamount to slighting the Creator. In Shia scholarship, this underscores the concept of 'Izzah' (honor) belonging to Allah and His servants, making social humiliation a theological offense rather than merely a social one. It serves as a foundational text for the etiquette of interaction among the faithful, warning that arrogance towards a believer disrupts one's spiritual alignment with the Divine.
